description: Mode A of the conversion story: the routine's whole Delphi unit becomes ONE C# file with the same types, the same routine names in the same order, and the same call graph — only syntax and casing become idiomatic. Free routines live on a static class named after the unit; every method carries a [SourceRoutine] attribute citing the unit, routine and line range it came from, and [SpecClaim] citations where a signed spec covers it. Types the unit takes from other units are stubbed under src/Stubs/ with a TODO until those units are converted. This archetype is the build shell (project files, provenance attributes, a test anchor) plus a shape exemplar (src/Unit.cs) the model imitates; the exemplar itself is never shipped in a generated package.

matches.fallback: Every Delphi routine: the unit that contains it is converted as a whole, with the routine's signed spec (and the unit's other signed specs) as guardrails.
